title: Prove the first deterministic Registry Context vertical
outcome: Establish one source-backed Goal Context for the Registry Context Project and prove that a local read-only resolver can turn an exact request for that Context into a deterministic immutable view while preserving source ownership, residue, compatibility limits, and authority_effect none.
rationale: CyberAlchemy agents need a reusable way to ask what Product, Project, Goal, Language, definitions, and source policies frame current work. A small proof must establish the meaning and exact construction chain before an interactive CLI, shared service, or broader registry runtime can be justified.
scope: one proposed Registry Context Project and one draft Goal
one CAV2-D66 Context that frames construction of Registry Context itself
one registry-backed Context specialization with exact request and immutable view contracts
one DomainSpec-v2 source, compiled graph, and system-ontology projection
one deterministic local read-only JSON CLI vertical
one bounded old-path migration and compatibility audit
exclusions: interactive wizard, chat synchronization, daemon, socket, database, cache, network, or container runtime
automatic discovery of repository paths or arbitrary source reads
source writes, owner decisions, lifecycle promotion, runtime adoption, or external effects
general proof that agents interpret or use the resolved context correctly
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Registry Context Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Registry Context runtime owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Context product owner

success_conditions.statement: Registry Context has one schema-valid Project, one linked Goal, and one linked CAV2-D66 Context with distinct identities.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The Project and Goal close bidirectionally; the Context names the Product, Project, Goal, consumer, and owner routes; every record retains authority_effect none.

success_conditions.statement: Registry Context crosses the CAV2-D65 construction sequence from product and business meaning through DomainSpec and compiled system ontology to implementation.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Exact stage identities and digests close without treating a hand-authored graph as compiler output or a passing local check as construction conformance.

success_conditions.statement: The resolver returns byte-identical schema-valid output twice for the same Context, request, and selected source bytes and blocks drift or unknown selections.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Golden two-run evidence plus negative cases for Context drift, source drift, unknown selection, path injection, missing binding, and authority escalation.

success_conditions.statement: The root migration preserves historical v1 evidence and exposes every known old-path consumer or compatibility limit.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A repository-wide reference inventory, migration manifest, legacy receipt preservation, and current v2 material receipt.

evidence_requirements: Project, Goal, Context, request, view, and runtime identities must remain distinct.
Only registered selection IDs may be resolved; arbitrary paths must fail closed.
A passing ontology, schema, or runtime test must not imply source authority, correct interpretation, adoption, release, or deployment.
Historical v1 receipts must remain immutable and visibly path-bound.

evidence_refs.claim_limit: Supports the CAV2-D66 meaning and identity boundary only; the Project record, Context instance, resolver, and migration require separate evidence.

target_horizon: first local proof vertical; no deployment deadline

revision_history.change: Created the Registry Context Project and first proof Goal before root migration, DomainSpec construction, or runtime implementation.
revision_history.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Registry Context Project owner

challenge_route: Challenge the desired product result and scope through the Registry Context Project owner, CAV2-D66 implications through definitions-governance and the Context product owner, construction claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, runtime evidence through the Registry Context runtime owner, and compatibility claims through affected consumer owners.
